title: Asyncio rate limiter with per-key buckets and a concurrency cap
prompt:
The new webhook dispatcher needs the asyncio limiter that ratelimit/limiter.py currently only stubs out. Please implement RateLimiter there so it behaves exactly as SPEC.md describes: a token bucket per key (rate, burst), a global cap on held slots (max_concurrent), FIFO order per key, the grant-pass rule for handing out slots across keys, and the cancellation rules, including undoing a grant when the waiting task is cancelled before acquire returns.

The public surface is the one in the stub: RateLimiter(rate, burst, max_concurrent, *, clock, sleep), async acquire(key), release(), limit(key) as an async context manager, the in_use property, tokens(key) and waiting(key=None). ValueError for bad constructor arguments and RuntimeError for a release() with nothing held.

Time only ever comes from the injected clock and only ever passes through the injected async sleep, which must be called with the exact delay until the next token as the spec says (no polling, no asyncio.sleep with a delay, no timeouts). tests/fake_time.py has the fake clock/sleep we use to drive this deterministically; please add tests for the limiter using it. TokenBucket in ratelimit/bucket.py can be reused or extended. Standard library only.
acceptance: Constructor validation, fresh state, RuntimeError on release; immediate acquires without sleep, exact token-wait sleep and refill timing, burst cap, FIFO per key, other keys not held up; concurrency cap with synchronous hand-over in release(), earliest caller across keys gets a freed slot, a key without tokens does not block the slot, limit() releases on error; cancellation of a sleeping head (next request takes over), of a slot waiter (nothing consumed), of a granted-but-not-returned request (slot freed, token refunded, next waiter granted), and the refunded token going to the same key's next request without time passing.
difficulty_rationale: Asyncio state machine with interacting per-key FIFO, cross-key slot ordering, timed waits through an injected sleep, and cancellation at two different stages including rollback of a grant; quick attempts usually miss the head hand-off or the grant rollback.
